# Cairn

> Cairn (npm: `cairn-engine`) is an open source agentic testing engine by Poem. You describe a browser task in plain language; Cairn uses AI to discover the steps once, freezes them as a JSON file, and replays that file on every later run without calling a model. When repair is explicitly enabled, Cairn attempts to repair a changed step with AI and saves the updated path only after verification. Application defects remain failures.

Landing page: https://team-poem.github.io/cairn-engine/ (English)
Korean landing page: https://team-poem.github.io/cairn-engine/ko/

## What it does
- Discover: turn a task description into concrete browser actions (log in, add to bag, open the cart) and save them as `*.skill.json`.
- Freeze: keep the path that worked so the next run follows the same steps.
- Replay: run the saved path deterministically. Basic replay makes no model calls, so it is cheap and stable in CI.
- Heal: opt-in AI repair for UI changes; save the updated path only after verification. Missing evidence in custom checks can be inconclusive and is not a pass.

## Architecture
A five-stage pipeline — Context, Plan, Execute, Judge, Report — where anything that varies comes in through a port:
- ContextProvider: appContext supplies app terminology and workflows to discovery, exploration, and repair. It guides AI but never replaces observed evidence or success checks. Healthy mechanical replay needs neither context nor a model.
- Planner: turns intent into a Scenario. A static planner replays a frozen file; an LLM loop discovers a new one.
- SkillStore: where frozen `*.skill.json` files live (a folder by default, or your own store).
- Driver: drives the browser and waits for the page to settle. Chrome DevTools ships; bring Playwright or your own.
- Critic: built-in critics judge execution and logic evidence. Screenshots are captured for records and host-defined custom checks, not judged by built-in critics. Custom checks with insufficient evidence can be inconclusive; missing proof is not a pass.
- Reporter: sends the result anywhere: console, JSON, or your team's tracker.

## Execution budgets
`budget: { maxModelCalls, timeoutMs }` limits model-call admissions and elapsed time per run, or per suite case across discovery and repair. Separate top-level calls have separate budgets. Timeouts are cooperative cancellation, not hard process termination or a billing cap. App context and execution budgets were introduced in 2.9.4; the 2.9.5 README expands their introduction.

## Install
- npm: `npm install cairn-engine`, then `npx cairn --help`
- pnpm: `pnpm add cairn-engine`, then `pnpm exec cairn --help`
- Yarn: `yarn add cairn-engine`, then `yarn exec cairn --help`
- Example with the npm local CLI: `npx cairn discover "log in, add a daypack, and open the cart" --url=https://your.app --freeze=cart.skill.json`

## Agentic testing reference
- English: https://team-poem.github.io/cairn-engine/agentic-testing/
- Korean: https://team-poem.github.io/cairn-engine/ko/agentic-testing/
These pages define browser agentic testing, its workflow, use cases, model-call boundaries, verification limits, and official sources. They describe testing web applications with an agent, not evaluating an AI model itself.
